root.name: Italian Game: Jerome Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. Bxf7+

overview: The Jerome Gambit plays 4.Bxf7+ Kxf7 and then 5.Nxe5+ Nxe5 6.d4 or 5.Nxe5+ Nxe5 6.Qh5+, giving up a bishop (and often a knight) for two pawns and the black king in the open. Black keeps the extra material and consolidates by returning at the right moment; the line is a club-level trap opening that strong players avoid. The attack is quick but not enough against correct play.

white_ideas.idea: Sacrifice the bishop on f7, follow with Nxe5+ and Qh5+ to drag the king into the open
Use d4 and the open lines to attack the exposed black king

black_ideas.idea: Take the sacrifices, keep the king safe on g8 after ...Ke6/...Kg8 and consolidate the extra piece
Trade queens and win the endgame a piece up

typical_structures.structure: White gets two pawns for a piece with an open centre; Black king exposed on f7 or e6

character.notes: A speculative sacrificial attack for the initiative: Sharp.

gambit.notes: 4.Bxf7+ Kxf7 gives a bishop for a pawn, and Black can keep the extra material.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound; Black wins with correct defence.

structure.notes: Open lines and an exposed king: Open.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play it; offbeat.

level.notes: Dubious lines are never Beginner; both sides need to calculate. Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Declining the sacrifice
sublines_that_differ.how: Black returns material and consolidates with ...Bd6 and ...Nc6, killing the attack.

character.reason: A piece sacrifice for an attack on the king in the open.

gambit.reason: White gives a bishop (and more) for two pawns.

structure.reason: Open centre and an exposed king.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play it.

level.reason: Short and tactical; Dubious so never Beginner.

plans.reason: The whole line is an attack on f7 and the king.
